rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 6 'What happened' line 52: 'The loop that started with a failing test closed.' 'The loop' has no antecedent earlier IN THIS FILE, but is arc-earned spine vocabulary: the rule's own carve-out lists 'the loop' by name as a non-violation example, and the host module (getting-going.md line 114: 'The loop's order is orient -> fix -> close -> compound') names it before this exercise's include. The noun phrase is also self-defining via its own relative clause ('that started with a failing test'). Stays inside. Chunk 0's 'the bug you fixed'/'the bug's ticket' (lines 5,7) and chunk 1's 'the bug you fixed' (line 13) resolve under the session-artifact carve-out ('the bug from prework' is a listed example). Chunk 4's 'it' (line 43, 'Does it sound like...') is immediate continuation of chunk 3's close-out subject (lines 33-39). Chunk 5's 'the next agent' (line 48) is ordinary generic phrasing for a future session, not an unresolved specific referent. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

Only external pointer in body: chunk 3 line 35, '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)' -- named by the document's own title, not located by page position (satisfies the navigational-pointer carve-out). No 'the opening lecture said' style backward callback to another file by position anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0/1 ('the bug you fixed', 'the bug's ticket', lines 5,7,13) and chunk 3's 'the PR' (line 39, inside the expanded prompt) resolve against fix-tests-first.md, verified as the exercise immediately preceding this one in the host module's include order (getting-going.md lines 46-48: 'Prove the bug, then ship the fix' -> 'Close the ticket' -> 'Compound and close'; line 114 confirms 'the close sits third on purpose'). This file's own Arc section (line 93) states 'Picks up from: fix-tests-first -- the shipped PR is what the close-out links to,' matching the module. No dead beat references found.

rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess/reveal construction anywhere in the file -- no live-demo beat present

rules_evaluated.evidence: Shortest chunk is 4 ('Double-check the voice', lines 41-44): its one bullet ('Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket? If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it.') carries a self-sufficient compare-and-correct instruction, not a bare wait-state. No chunk in the seven-chunk deck (incl. title) is context-dependent-only.

Checked all six body headers against their chunk content: 'Read the ticket for your bug' -> opens+pastes ticket link (11-19); 'Read the conventions off the ticket' -> field-convention read + five-rule ask (20-31); 'Write the close-out and send it' -> drafts+posts close-out (33-40); 'Double-check the voice' -> register check (41-44); 'Anything can be reverse-engineered' -> generalises the move, declarative per rule 15's named exception (45-49); 'What happened' -> recap (50-55). Closest-to-violating: chunk 5's declarative header against line 47's supporting claim -- header and content agree, no contradiction.

Scanned all seven chunks against all six sub-patterns via `grep -niE '\bnot\b' curriculum/evals/body-views/ae101--exercise--close-the-ticket.body.txt` (2 hits: line 23 'not the policy', line 47 'you did not write' -- single negations, no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple). Anaphora/epistrophe triples: none. Self-grading superlative (blocking sub-item): closest line is chunk 3 line 35, '...and it pays back on every session after this one' -- a factual persistence claim about an installed connector, not graded language; stays inside. Number+retraction: none (plain counts only: '20 minutes', 'five bug rules', neither hedged). Abstraction-noun stacks: none -- vocabulary stays concrete (ticket, tracker, connector, close-out). Empty-leg verb triplets: none.
